Four frontier models launched in a single week. The pricing war that follows will reshape every enterprise AI budget in 2027.

GPT-6 Astra went live September 3 with no published price. Claude Fable 5.1 arrived on AWS at $10/$50. Google shipped Gemini 3.8 Flash at $0.75/$3.75 intro pricing. Meta dropped Muse Spark 1.3 at roughly $0.10 per million tokens — the cheapest model in the leaderboard's top five.

The monthly cadence of major AI model releases has roughly quadrupled since 2023. That compression changes the calculus for every CTO locking into AI vendor contracts.

Three strategic implications stand out. First, model switching costs are the new vendor lock-in — architect for portability now or pay the integration tax later. Second, pricing is in free fall at the inference layer, which means the value capture shifts decisively to application logic and workflow orchestration. Third, the gap between open-weight and proprietary performance is narrowing fast, and procurement strategies that ignore open-weight options are leaving leverage on the table.

The executive decision is no longer which model to bet on. It is how to build an AI architecture that absorbs the next frontier release without a re-engineering cycle.
